body:
61% of the top 1% of LinkedIn posts put a real number in the first two lines.

That comes from a study of 438,413 posts. The pattern is not a clever hook. It is a count, a percent or a price, from a named source.

Opening with a precise number lifted median likes 17%. Opening with a question cut them 28%. Same idea, different first line.

So before you post, read your first line. If there is no number in it, find the one fact you can count.

Today, rewrite the first line of your next post so it starts with a number you can source.

Source: LinkPost study of 438,413 posts, Jul 2026 — https://www.linkpost.gg/en/playbooks/linkedin-algorithm-playbook-2026/study
action: rewrite the first line of your next post so it starts with a number you can source
second_comment: The same study found the question opener is the one most people reach for first. It cut median likes 28%.
